original_question: Consider synchronization over SO(2) or over a finite group, with signal elements sampled uniformly over group elements, and fix a number of frequencies L that does not depend on n. In the computationally hard regime lambda in (lambda_stat, 1), does there exist a sub-exponential-time detection algorithm, specifically running in time exp(n^delta) for some delta < 1, that can reliably detect the signal as n -> infinity?
target_in_paper: Entry 4, Open Problem 8 — Detection in Multi-Frequency synchronization
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper’s intended target very closely: it asks about the multi-frequency synchronization model over SO(2) or a finite group, with the signal sampled uniformly over group elements, in the fixed-L regime, in the computationally hard interval λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1), and it asks whether there is a sub-exponential detector of runtime exp(n^δ) with δ < 1 that succeeds reliably as n → ∞.
missing_details: The paper’s model is the dense all-pairs observation model with additive Gaussian noise; this is implicit in your draft but should be stated explicitly to make the question stand-alone.
In the SO(2) formulation, the L channels are Y_ell = (λ/n)x^(ell)(x^(ell))* + n^(-1/2)W^(ell), with independent Gaussian noise matrices W^(1),...,W^(L) and x^(ell) = (x_1^ell,...,x_n^ell).

In the finite-group formulation, the 'frequencies' are representation-theoretic channels from the Peter-Weyl decomposition: Y_kj^ρ = (λ/n)ρ(g_k)ρ(g_j^(-1)) + n^(-1/2)W_kj^(ρ) for ρ in a fixed set Ψ of size L.
The paper is asking a detection problem, i.e. distinguishing the planted model from the corresponding null all-noise model; your draft says 'detect the signal' but does not state the null explicitly.
The quantifier over λ should be made explicit: the paper-faithful reading is for each fixed λ in the hard regime λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1), not merely for some unspecified λ in that interval.

The sentence immediately preceding Open Problem 8 suggests that the sub-exponential runtime may depend on the signal strength, so one should not silently require one uniform exponent δ for the entire interval unless that stronger version is intended.
Your draft does not explicitly say that measurements are available for all pairs (j, k), which is part of the setup in Entry 4.
The symbol λ_stat should be identified as the statistical/information-theoretic detection threshold of the corresponding multi-frequency model.

If one wants to match the nearby hardness discussion exactly, one should say whether the finite group is fixed as n grows; the motivation immediately before the open problem discusses SO(2) or finite groups of constant size.
refined_question: Fix either G = SO(2) (equivalently U(1)) or a fixed finite group G. Consider the dense multi-frequency synchronization model from Entry 4, where measurements are available for every pair (j, k) and, for a fixed collection Ψ of L frequency/representation channels with L independent of n, the planted observation is Y_kj^ρ = (λ/n)ρ(g_k)ρ(g_j^(-1)) + n^(-1/2)W_kj^(ρ) for ρ in Ψ (in the SO(2) case, equivalently, Y_ell = (λ/n)x^(ell)(x^(ell))* + n^(-1/2)W^(ell) for ell = 1,...,L), with g = (g_1,...,g_n) sampled uniformly from G^n and Gaussian noise W. For every fixed signal-to-noise ratio λ in the computationally hard regime λ ∈ (λ_stat, 1), where λ_stat is the statistical detection threshold and 1 is the spectral threshold, does there exist a possibly λ-dependent algorithm running in time exp(n^δ) for some δ < 1 that distinguishes the planted model from the corresponding null all-noise model with error probability o(1) as n → ∞?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Open Problem 8, not Open Problem 7. Open Problem 7 asks for a scaling L = L_n that would permit polynomial-time detection below the spectral threshold, whereas your draft fixes L and asks instead for sub-exponential detection in the hard regime. I therefore kept the scope exactly at Open Problem 8 and only inserted the paper’s implicit setup needed for a stand-alone formulation: the dense Gaussian multi-frequency observation model, the planted-versus-null meaning of detection, the representation-theoretic meaning of 'frequencies' for finite groups, and the fact that the runtime exponent may depend on the signal strength.
